entries.title: glTF animation of rigid (non-skinned) meshes parented to bone nodes is ignored
entries.missing: assets/models/robot.glb (RobotExpressive style) animates by moving node transforms: every body part is a plain mesh child of a bone node and only the two hands are skinned. The Animator only drives skins, so the model stayed frozen in bind pose in every clip (identical screenshots at frames 5, 12, 18, 30 with Running). This layout is very common (three.js examples, many CC0 character packs, Blender exports without weight painting). No warning is printed.
entries.workaround: Wrote a Python script (tools/skinify.py) that bakes every rigid mesh into model space, gives it JOINTS_0/WEIGHTS_0 = 100% its parent bone and builds a skin with inverse bind matrices; then the Animator plays it. [P2] The same happens with Kenney cube-pets animal-dog.glb, where the MESH nodes themselves are the animated bones (8 clips, no skin): the dog stood frozen in every clip. tools/skinify.py now also treats an animated mesh node as its own bone (7 joints), and the Animator then plays walk/run/idle. Second asset of two in this game with the same layout, so it is common in CC0 packs.
entries.suggestion: Support node-transform animation of non-skinned mesh nodes in the Animator (drive the node world matrix of a MeshRenderer model's nodes), or auto-convert rigid-per-bone meshes to a skin at load. At least print a warning when a model has clips but no skin.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.4 (Rigid glTF animation and several skins) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/rigid-animation (M26.4): a mesh that is a child of an animated node, or an animated mesh node with no skin, follows its node through a rigid skin the importer makes (parse_skeleton), so the Animator plays RobotExpressive and the Kenney cube pets as exported; a model with clips that nothing can play logs one warning naming them. The game imports the original robot.glb (hands included) and animal-dog.glb again and tools/skinify.py is gone.

entries.title: glTF with two skins sharing the same joints: second skin is drawn wrong, no way to fix without editing the file
entries.missing: robot.glb has two skins (one per hand) with identical joint lists and inverse bind matrices. Only the first is animated; the hand meshes of the second skin were drawn displaced (large curved shape hanging off the arm) in the Idle pose. The warning says 'drawn in bind pose, not animated' but the result is a visibly broken mesh, not a bind pose.
entries.workaround: Dropped the two hand meshes from the glb in the same script (the arms end in balls anyway).
entries.suggestion: Merge skins that have the same joints/IBMs at load, or animate every skin of the file; the 'first skin' limit is a trap for exported characters.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.4 (Rigid glTF animation and several skins) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/rigid-animation (M26.4): every mesh is drawn with the palette of its own skin (Animator::skinPalettes, one per glTF skin), so the two hand skins of the original robot.glb animate; the 'first skin only' limit and its warning are gone. The game imports the original robot.glb with both hands.

entries.title: No command to scaffold the menu kit; it can only be extracted from the docs by hand
entries.missing: factoria docs read menus lists about 18 files (menu stack, settings, pause menu, options, prefabs, scenes, locales) to copy, but there is no `project.add_menu_kit` or similar. A game-making AI has to parse the markdown fences itself.
entries.workaround: Wrote a small script that splits the doc's fenced blocks (```lang path) into files.
entries.suggestion: Add a command (and MCP tool) that writes the kit into the project, optionally with a choice of parts (pause only, settings only).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.22 (Menu kit command) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: validate keeps the audio loudness warnings after defaults.audio.normalize is set
entries.missing: assets.json has "defaults": {"audio": {"normalize": true}} as the validate hint suggests, yet `factoria validate` still warns that pluck_001.ogg peaks at 0.4 dBFS and toggle_001.ogg differs by 12.5 LU from click_001.ogg. Either the default is not applied to the check or only to playback; it is unclear which.
entries.workaround: Left the two warnings (they are not errors). [P2] P2 sounds: validate still warns for loopcity_0.ogg (peaks at 0.3 dBFS), pluck_001.ogg and toggle_001.ogg (loudness) although assets.json sets normalize: true for them; the warning should read the import settings.
entries.suggestion: Make the loudness check read the effective import settings (defaults merged with per-asset), or say in the warning that the default is already applied and the warning is about the source file.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.5 (Model import and asset tooling) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/model-import (M26.5): validate's loudness warnings use the gain defaults.audio.normalize applies (peak and LUFS after the gain). The project now sets defaults.audio.targetLufs -20, because the peak-limited click_001.ogg cannot reach -16 and the spread of effects was still over 12 LU.

entries.title: Test API cannot hold a mouse button or turn the wheel, so mouse drag orbit and wheel zoom are untestable end to end
entries.missing: game.touch* and keyDown exist, but there is no game.mouseDown/mouseMove/mouseUp or game.wheel(dy) in factoria:test. A follow camera that orbits with a mouse drag and zooms with the wheel can only be tested by calling its own orbit()/zoom() methods, not through the input path.
entries.workaround: tests/camera.test.js calls orbit() and zoom() directly; the drag and wheel reading in follow_camera.js readInput() has no test.
entries.suggestion: Add game.mouse(x, y), game.mouseDown(button), game.mouseUp(button) and game.wheel(dy) to the test API (same as game.input mouse/buttons).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: Validator flags a method named start() as a lifecycle-hook lookalike
entries.missing: A class method `start(seconds)` on a plain helper Behaviour (the spring timer) triggers 'method start() is not a lifecycle hook' although it is a normal method called from another script. A natural name for a timer API.
entries.workaround: Renamed it to fill().
entries.suggestion: Only warn for names that differ from a hook by case or prefix (OnStart, onstart, on_start), not for generic verbs like start.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: Entity animator facade does not expose the parameter values
entries.missing: entity.animator has state and setters but no values; tests had to read get("Animator").values to assert speed/grounded parameters.
entries.workaround: tests/animator.test.js uses game.find(id).get("Animator").values.
entries.suggestion: Expose animator.values (read-only) or animator.get(name) on the facade.
notes: Fixed in e3ab260 (before this report): entity.animator.get(name) returns a parameter's current value (a declared param or a set one; a wrong name throws with a "did you mean"), and game.find(id) in a test returns the same entity, so tests/animator.test.js can read game.find(id).animator.get("speed"). docs/ANIMATION.md now shows it (m26/triage).

entries.title: assets.import of a .glb does not copy the texture file it references
entries.missing: Importing Kenney .glb models (fantasy-town-kit, platformer-kit, cube-pets) with assets.import copies only the .glb. The files reference an external image (uri 'Textures/colormap.png') and rendering then logs 'texture file not found: assets/models/Textures/colormap.png' and draws untextured. The error is only visible at render time (not in the import result nor in validate). Worse: three kits ship DIFFERENT colormap.png files under the same relative name, so importing two kits into assets/models/ silently makes them collide.
entries.workaround: Moved each kit into its own folder (assets/models/town, props, pets), copied that kit's Textures/colormap.png next to it by hand and re-keyed assets.json (with provenance for the png).
entries.suggestion: assets.import for .glb/.gltf should copy every external uri it references (keeping the relative layout under a folder named after the model or the pack), add provenance for them, and warn when the destination folder already holds a different file of the same name. validate should report a model whose external texture is missing.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.5 (Model import and asset tooling) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/model-import (M26.5): assets.import of a .glb or .gltf copies the textures and buffers its uris point at (with provenance), shares an identical file already there and warns when a DIFFERENT file of the same name is (import each kit into its own folder); factoria validate reports a model whose texture is missing. The kit folders under assets/models stay: they are the layout the warning recommends.

entries.title: No path finding or navmesh for 3D characters
entries.missing: Guard dogs that chase the courier around walls, and tap-to-move, need a path over the level geometry. The engine has no navmesh, no grid and no A*; a game AI has to write its own from physics queries.
entries.workaround: scripts/nav.js: a lazy height-field grid over the physics world (a ray straight down for the ground height, physics.overlapSphere for obstacles, a step-height rule for connections, A* with line-of-sight smoothing). It works but is slow to write, must be rebuilt when a gate or crate moves, and cannot know about doors or one-way drops.
entries.suggestion: A `nav.findPath(from, to, {radius, stepHeight})` API (and a NavGrid/navmesh component baked from static colliders, with a dirty flag for moving obstacles) next to physics.raycast3d.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.10 (Navmesh and paths for 3D) in feedback/ROADMAP.md (M19's navmesh, taken now that a game needs it).

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/navmesh (M26.10): a NavMesh3D component baked from the static colliders (agentRadius, agentHeight, stepHeight, maxSlope), nav.findPath(from, to, {radius}) in scripts and the nav.find_path / nav.bake / nav.info commands, Collider3D.navObstacle for gates and crates that move, and "Show navmesh" in the editor (docs/NAVIGATION.md). The game's scripts/nav.js, dog.js and tap_move.js still use their own grid: moving them onto the engine API needs the six levels re-tuned and retested, which is a game task.

entries.title: A CharacterController3D is not carried by a kinematic platform it stands on
entries.missing: Kinematic RigidBody3D platforms carry dynamic bodies, but a character standing on one stays put and slides off as the platform moves. Moving platforms are a staple of 3D platformers.
entries.workaround: scripts/courier.js reads the velocity of the kinematic body under its feet (the ground entity of the last move) and adds it to its own move every frame; scripts/mover.js drives the platform by velocity only, so the numbers agree.
entries.suggestion: physics.moveCharacter should add the displacement of the kinematic body it is grounded on (the way it already treats dynamic bodies), with an option to turn it off.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.2 (Character controller on moving and dynamic bodies) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/character-platforms (M26.2): a character on a kinematic platform is carried with its displacement and turn (CharacterController3D.carriedByPlatforms), so courier.js and mover.js no longer add the platform velocity.

entries.title: Characters do not weigh on dynamic bodies and push them aside
entries.missing: A CharacterController3D is kinematic: standing on a dynamic plank, seesaw or rope bridge applies no force to it, and walking into one shoves it along the ground (it slid a seesaw off its pivot). Seesaws, rope bridges and sinking platforms cannot work with the real character.
entries.workaround: scripts/seesaw.js simulates the weight: while the courier is grounded on the plank the hinge motor drives the end it stands on down, and the plank's own velocity is zeroed every fixed step so the courier cannot push it off its pivot. scripts/rope_bridge.js lets the planks be walked on without reacting to the load (heavy damping keeps it calm).
entries.suggestion: Let the character controller optionally apply its weight (mass x gravity) to the dynamic body below, and expose `pushStrength` or a layer rule so it does not shove bodies that are jointed.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.2 (Character controller on moving and dynamic bodies) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/character-platforms (M26.2): CharacterController3D.applyWeight / mass press on the dynamic body below and pushStrength never shoves a jointed one, so seesaw.js and rope_bridge.js lost their weight workarounds.

entries.title: Scene loads are synchronous and there is no progress or preload API
entries.missing: A loading screen cannot show real progress: scene.load blocks the frame, there is no way to load or warm up assets in steps (models, textures, audio), and no event when they are ready.
entries.workaround: scenes/loading.scene.json draws a step bar that counts the three frames the script really runs before the blocking scene.load; it is honest about being steps, not a percentage.
entries.suggestion: scene.preload(path) returning a handle with progress 0..1 (loading assets on a worker), or scene.loadAsync plus an `onProgress` callback; the same for assets.preload([paths]).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.7 (Scene and asset preload with progress) in feedback/ROADMAP.md (M19's scene.loadAsync, taken now that a game needs it).

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/scene-preload (M26.7): `scene.preload(path)` and `assets.preload(paths)` return a handle with `progress`, `done` and a `promise`; the work is cut into files, four per frame in tests and a few ms per frame in a window; the scene.load that follows reads nothing from the disk. scripts/loading.js now shows the real progress and scripts/intro.js preloads the title screen.

entries.title: No animal sounds (bark, growl) in the CC0 sound kits the engine suggests
entries.missing: The guard dog needs a bark. The Kenney kits in the docs have impacts, interface sounds and jingles but nothing animal, and there is no sound generator command.
entries.workaround: A pitched heavy impact (impactPunch_heavy_000.ogg) stands in for the bark; the dog also flashes a red view cone and shows an exclamation mark, so the warning does not depend on sound.
entries.suggestion: Document a CC0 animal/creature pack in the assets guide, or add an `audio.synth` helper (noise burst plus filtered sweep) for simple barks, growls and whooshes.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.5 (Model import and asset tooling) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/model-import (M26.5): assets.synth_sound {path, preset, seed} makes a deterministic bark, growl, meow and the usual effects offline; the guard dog now plays assets/audio/dog_bark.wav (preset bark) and the borrowed impactPunch_heavy_000.ogg is gone.

entries.title: Joint3D connected empty string is rejected by the scene validator but documented as 'the world'
entries.missing: The Joint3D field doc says `Empty = the world`, but a scene or spawn with "connected": "" fails validation. The field has to be left out.
entries.workaround: scripts/rope_bridge.js only sets `connected` when there is a next plank; the last plank's joint omits the field.
entries.suggestion: Accept the empty string as the world (as documented), or change the doc to say 'leave the field out'.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.14 (Joints: overlaps, rest and bridges) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/joints (M26.14): gates and joints read `stalled` and `connected: ""` means the world.

entries.title: A joint-driven body is silently stopped by an overlapping static collider
entries.missing: A hinge gate whose swept volume touched a static wall by a few centimetres did not open, with no warning. The motor pushed against the wall forever.
entries.workaround: Levels leave 0.2 m of clearance around every hinge gate and the arena's gate sits between two walls with that gap.
entries.suggestion: A validate or debug-draw warning when a Joint3D body overlaps a static collider it is not connected to at the start pose, or a `game_state` field listing joints that are stalled against the motor.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; CC/FB-0053 merged here (the same missing warning, met when a body starts inside a static collider); work package M26.14 (Joints: overlaps, rest and bridges) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/joints (M26.14): a body started inside a static collider is logged once and reported by validate.

entries.title: scene.format without paths rewrites every scene and prefab of the project
entries.missing: `factoria call scene.format` with no arguments reformatted the whole project (every scene and prefab), turning a one-file edit into a huge diff. Nothing in the command's description warns about it.
entries.workaround: Always pass `{"paths": [...]}`; level generators write canonical JSON themselves and the project notes say never to run it bare.
entries.suggestion: Make `paths` required (or default to `check: true`), and print how many files it will change before writing more than a few.
notes: 2026-10-22: Always pass explicit paths; reverted the three files with git and re-applied only the edits.
2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.1 (Commands write only what they change) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/commands-write-only (M26.1): `scene.format` without `paths`, `all` or `check` writes nothing and fails naming `paths` and `all` (the first files it would change).

entries.title: A chain of hinged planks rings for a long time; a rope bridge needs heavy damping and wide planks
entries.missing: A rope bridge built from dynamic planks joined by Joint3D hinges swung by about 1 m unloaded with the default damping and was unstable with planks narrower than 2 m. A bridge should be a one-line component, not a tuning exercise.
entries.workaround: scripts/rope_bridge.js uses linearDamping 3 and angularDamping 8, width 2 m, sag 0.35 and 9 planks; with these it hangs still and holds the courier.
entries.suggestion: A `Rope`/`Chain` component (or solver iterations per joint chain) that is stable by default, or a documented recipe for bridges in the physics guide.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.14 (Joints: overlaps, rest and bridges) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/joints (M26.14): jointed chains sleep as islands and CCD is solved per island.

entries.title: scene.load called from a test only takes effect in the next frame
entries.missing: In a test, `scene.load(path)` changes scene.current at once but the new scene's scripts start only on the next step, so reading their state right after the call gives the old values. game.load() and in-game scene.load calls behave differently, which is easy to trip over.
entries.workaround: tests step two frames after scene.load before reading anything.
entries.suggestion: Document the difference in the testing guide, or make scene.load from a test start the scene immediately like game.load.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: scene.load from a test is deferred on purpose (it runs at the start of the next frame, as in a game) and game.load is immediate; what is missing is saying so in SCRIPTING.md, "Tests": work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: No calendar date API and no way to pin the date in tests
entries.missing: A daily route (a different challenge each calendar day) needs the real date. The scripting API has no `time.today` or similar; the only source is the JS `Date`, which reads the wall clock (the docs tell games never to use Date.now) and has no test hook: `factoria:test` cannot set the date, so a test of date-driven behaviour is either flaky or impossible. The docs say nothing about how a game should get the date.
entries.workaround: scripts/clock.js is the only place that reads `new Date()`; everything else asks clock.today(), and tests pin the day with clock.setToday() (stored in `session`). Dates are YYYY-MM-DD of the local day.
entries.suggestion: Add `time.calendar()` (or `game.today()`) returning {year, month, day, utcOffsetMinutes, iso} from the real clock, recorded in replays, plus `game.setDate("2026-10-22")` in factoria:test (and a --date flag for headless runs) so date-driven logic is deterministic. Document the rule in the scripting guide next to rng.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.3 (Calendar date and app lifecycle) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/calendar-lifecycle (M26.3): game.today() gives the real local date in a player, a fixed one in tests and headless runs, the recorded one in a replay; game.setDate and --date choose it.

entries.title: No on-screen keyboard for gamepad players
entries.missing: A first-run name screen must work with a gamepad alone (TV, handheld, desktop without a keyboard). A focused TextField raises the phone's own keyboard (docs/MOBILE.md, 'The on-screen keyboard'), but there is nothing for a gamepad: no virtual keyboard widget, no call to a platform one (Steam's, a console's), so the game cannot take a name without keys.
entries.workaround: profile.scene.json has a grid of 36 buttons built at runtime (key_A..key_9, space, delete) that edit the TextField text; d-pad focus walks the grid.
entries.suggestion: A built-in virtual keyboard widget a TextField can open when focus came from a gamepad (letters, digits, space, delete, done; d-pad navigation; localised layouts), and `input.showKeyboard` calling the platform's own gamepad keyboard where one exists (Steam Big Picture, consoles).
notes: 2026-10-23: Fixed in M26.17: a focused TextField raises the phone's keyboard; docs/MENUS.md has an on-screen keyboard kit (prefab, script, test) for gamepad players. The Steam Deck's own keyboard stays with M12.
2026-10-22: The name field accepts the system keyboard on a PC and phone; the letter grid stays Latin.

2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open, and verifying it found a bug: a focused TextField does not raise the phone's keyboard (only input.showKeyboard does), although docs/MOBILE.md says it does. Both are work package M26.17 (Text entry on every device) in feedback/ROADMAP.md; the Steam Deck's own keyboard is M12's, with Steamworks.

entries.title: A localized Text cannot take parameters and is rewritten every frame
entries.missing: Text.key looks up a fixed string and rewrites it every frame, so text with a name, a time or a count (Delivered, Ana! / Time: 41.5 s) cannot use a key. Writing text in a script is overwritten unless key is cleared first.
entries.workaround: Scripts clear Text.key and write the string built from i18n.t with replacements (level_flow.setText, results_view.js, level_select.js).
entries.suggestion: Text.keyArgs (an object of replacements) or a {name} placeholder filled from a bound value, re-localized on language change.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; CC/FB-0027 merged here (the same missing keyArgs, met on a Button, plus validate's warning on keys with placeholders); work package M26.12 (Localized text with parameters) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/i18n-args (M26.12): Text, Button, Toggle, Slider, TextField and TouchButton take keyArgs (the values of the key's {placeholders}); the engine formats the key with them when the text is localized and after a language switch, so a script sets keyArgs once. The HUD parcel counter, the results heading and time lines and the paint shop's texts use it; the results spring line (several translated lines with marks) stays one string.

entries.title: Default UI font has no star glyph
entries.missing: Star ratings need a filled and an empty star; the built-in font only has ASCII, so a star symbol renders as a missing glyph.
entries.workaround: Stars are drawn as * (earned) and - (missing) in results_view.starText.
entries.suggestion: Ship a symbols font or a Rating widget (n of max, filled/empty sprites).
notes: Fixed before this report, documented in m26/triage: the built-in DejaVu Sans has ★ (U+2605) and ☆ (U+2606), and ✓ ✗ ♥ ♪ ← →; colour emoji such as ⭐ (U+2B50) are not in it, which is likely the missing glyph seen. docs/TEXT.md now says so. results_view.starText can use ★ and ☆.

entries.title: No way to share a UI panel between scenes
entries.missing: The results and retry panels are copied into all eight level scenes; changing one means editing eight files. UI prefabs with child text overrides were not an obvious fit.
entries.workaround: The layout stays duplicated; texts are written at runtime from one script (results_view.js).
entries.suggestion: Document or support UI prefabs with child overrides, or a scene include, in the menus guide.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: a prefab already shares a panel between scenes (each scene instances it); what is missing is the recipe in MENUS.md and per-instance overrides of a prefab's children: work package M26.20 (Scene tree: sibling order and shared panels) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/scene-order (M26.20): a prefab reference takes `overrides` (child id, name or path -> name, tags, active, components) and world.spawnPrefab takes `childOverrides`; docs/MENUS.md has the recipe ("A panel shared between scenes"). The game's eight level scenes still hold their own copies of the panels: moving them onto one prefab is a game task.

entries.title: The fake store cannot simulate a refund or a revoked purchase
entries.missing: purchases.restore() on the fake keeps every non-consumable forever, so the path 'the store no longer lists a product I own' (refund, Family Sharing removed) cannot be driven from a test. game.platform.reset() wipes everything, which is the only way to emulate it.
entries.workaround: store.reconcile({authoritative:true}) revokes products the store no longer lists; tests call game.platform.reset() and then reconcile. On the fake backend the start-up reconcile is not authoritative (a dev run would lose its purchases at each start).
entries.suggestion: game.platform.revoke(productId) (and an equivalent dev command) that removes the product from restore() and emits no event, like the Apple 'refunded transaction is never delivered' rule.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: the fake answers purchases as scripted, but nothing takes a finished purchase back: work package M26.8 (Store fake and catalog in scripts) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/store-fake (M26.8): game.platform.revoke(id) (command platform.revoke) takes a purchase back and sends the "purchase" event with status "revoked"; restore() no longer lists it. shop.test.js drives a real refund and store.listen() takes the product away.

entries.title: purchases.finish() throws synchronously for an unknown transaction instead of rejecting
entries.missing: Every other platform call returns a Promise that rejects, but purchases.finish(id) with an id the game was not told about throws at the call, so `await platform.purchases.finish(id).catch(...)` does not catch it.
entries.workaround: store.grant wraps the call in try/await/catch.
entries.suggestion: Return a rejected Promise with the same message and hint, like the rest of the platform API.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.8 (Store fake and catalog in scripts) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/store-fake (M26.8): purchases.finish() of an unknown transaction rejects with code unknownId, so store.grant uses .catch() instead of try/await.

entries.title: storage and the platform fake keep their state between tests of a run
entries.missing: storage.set data and the fake store (owned products, unlocks, delayFrames, backend) survive from one test to the next and from one file to the next, so each test must clean up by hand; one forgotten key makes a later file fail only in the full run.
entries.workaround: tests/helpers/store.js: fresh() before and cleanup() after every test.
entries.suggestion: An option (or the default) that clears storage and resets game.platform before each test, or game.resetState().
notes: 2026-10-22: tests/helpers/store.js: fresh() before and cleanup() after every test.
2026-10-22 (clockwork-courier-p5): module state, session, game.paused and the language leak too; tests/comfort.test.js resets them in afterEach.

2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: each test file already starts clean (storage, the platform fake and module state are reset between files); tests in one file share them. A reset between tests is work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: A Button or Text with `key` loses its dynamic text, and keys with {placeholders} warn in validate
entries.missing: The locale system rewrites the text of every entity that has `key` each frame, so a button whose label is built from state (price, count, 'Equip/Equipped') must have no key at all, and then validate cannot check its text against the locales; a key with {price} placeholders on a component is a warning.
entries.workaround: The dynamic buttons of the shop have no `key`; scripts/ui/shop.js sets the text with i18n.t(key, args) at every refresh.
entries.suggestion: A `keyArgs` object (or a Text/Button `args` field scripts can set) so the engine formats the key with placeholders.
notes: 2026-10-22: The dynamic buttons of the shop have no `key`; scripts/ui/shop.js sets the text with i18n.t(key, args) at every refresh.

2026-10-22 triage: duplicate of FB-0021 (keyArgs on localized widgets; its occurrences were merged there); validate's check of placeholders against keyArgs is part of work package M26.12 (Localized text with parameters) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/i18n-args (M26.12): keyArgs on Button (see FB-0021) and factoria validate now checks a key's placeholders against the entity's keyArgs: it warns only for a placeholder with no arg or an arg no translation uses. The shop's dynamic buttons use key and keyArgs.

entries.title: No ads API: no rewarded ad, no consent or tracking-permission flow, no dev/release flag
entries.missing: A game that offers a rewarded ad ("watch to get 20 s more") has nothing in the engine to show one with: no ad provider interface, no user-consent (GDPR/UMP) or App Tracking Transparency flow, no way to know whether this is a development or a release build (so a test ad stub cannot be switched off for the store build), no 'ad loaded' state.
entries.workaround: scripts/ads.js defines the provider interface (name, available(), showRewarded(placement) -> {rewarded, reason}) and a stub overlay (scripts/ad_stub.js) used only while platform.backend is 'fake'; any other backend has no provider and the retry screen shows no ad offer. A real SDK plugin would call ads.setProvider().
entries.suggestion: A platform.ads service next to purchases: ads.available(placement), ads.showRewarded(placement) -> {rewarded}, ads.consent() (with the ATT/UMP sheets) and a platform.release boolean; the fake backend answers with a scripted test ad so games and tests share one path.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; the API, the catalog's placements, consent and platform.release with the fake backend are work package M26.9 (Ads and leaderboard periods: the API and the fake) in feedback/ROADMAP.md; the real backends (Google UMP and AdMob, Apple ATT, the GDPR/COPPA screen) are M12's next package.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/ads-periods (M26.9): platform.ads (available, showRewarded, consent), the catalog's platform.ads.placements and platform.release; the fake shows a scripted test ad (game.platform.ad). scripts/ad_stub.js is gone, scripts/ads.js and more_time.js sit on platform.ads. The real networks (UMP, AdMob, ATT) are M12's next package.

entries.title: Catalog is not readable from scripts and leaderboards have no localizable name
entries.missing: game.project.platform (the catalog of factoria.json) is not exposed to scripts, so the code must repeat the product types (consumable or not) and the ids; achievements and products have titleKey/descriptionKey but a leaderboard has only a plain `name`, so the in-game board titles are a second copy in the locale files.
entries.workaround: scripts/store.js keeps a TYPES table; the leaderboards screen builds its titles from the level name keys; a test compares the code's lists with game.platform.state().catalog.
entries.suggestion: platform.catalog (read only: ids, types, titles) and nameKey on leaderboards.
notes: 2026-10-22: Board titles are built from the level-name keys of the locale files (board.time, board.daily, board.stars), as in P4.

2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: the catalog is already readable as game.project.platform, but undocumented, and leaderboards have no localizable name: work package M26.8 (Store fake and catalog in scripts) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/store-fake (M26.8): game.project.platform is documented and store.js reads product types from it (no TYPES table); leaderboards take a nameKey, resolved in the current language in the request the backend gets. The board screen keeps its parameterized titles (board.time with the level name), which one key cannot express.

entries.title: No per-day or per-season leaderboards: the catalog is static
entries.missing: A 'daily route' board must be a new board every day, but boards are declared in factoria.json and Game Center / Steam create them by hand. There is no board id suffix, reset period or season in the catalog.
entries.workaround: One 'daily_route' board holds the best time ever; the day is only in the daily_route_finished event.
entries.suggestion: A `period` (daily, weekly) on a leaderboard that the backends map to their recurring boards, or leaderboards.submit(id, score, {suffix: date}).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; periods in the catalog, the API and the fake are work package M26.9 (Ads and leaderboard periods: the API and the fake) in feedback/ROADMAP.md; periods on the real store backends are M12's.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/ads-periods (M26.9): a leaderboard takes period allTime, daily or weekly; the fake keeps one board per game.today() day or week. daily_route is now period daily and services.js needs nothing else. Periods on the real stores are M12's.

entries.title: MeshRenderer tints the whole model: no per-material colour
entries.missing: A paint scheme for the robot (the glTF has an orange body, dark eyes, grey metal) can only multiply every material by one colour and add one emissive, so the base orange limits the palette (mint needed a dark tint plus a strong emissive to read as teal) and the eyes change colour too.
entries.workaround: scripts/paints.js stores a dark tint plus an emissive per paint, tuned by looking at screenshots.
entries.suggestion: MeshRenderer.materialColors: {materialName: [r,g,b,a]} overrides, or a colour per glTF material slot.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.16 (Per-material colours) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: No control over the sibling order of a spawned UI child
entries.missing: world.spawn(json, {parent}) always appends, so a button added at run time to a Panel with a column layout lands below the existing ones; the layout follows the hierarchy order.
entries.workaround: scripts/more_time.js spawns the new button and then calls setParent again on the two stock buttons so they come after it.
entries.suggestion: A `index` (or `before`) option in world.spawn's options and entity.setParent(parent, index).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.20 (Scene tree: sibling order and shared panels) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/scene-order (M26.20): world.spawn(json, {parent, index}), world.spawnPrefab(path, {parent, index}), entity.setParent(parent, keepWorld, index) and scene.set_parent {index}. scripts/more_time.js still re-parents the stock buttons: a game task to drop.

entries.title: The result of a physics scene depends on which tests ran before it in the same run
entries.missing: tests/levels.test.js plays the main route of rooftops_3 (rope bridge) with the waypoint bot: it needs 2815 frames when the file runs alone and 2009 after other test files, with nothing in the project reading the previous tests' state (every play() reloads the scene and clears the save). Same scene, same input, different physics, so a test that compares two runs flips with the order and number of earlier tests.
entries.workaround: The 'shortcut is not slower' check allows 300 frames of tolerance.
entries.suggestion: game.load() should rebuild the physics world and reseed world.rng exactly like a first load (or document which state survives).
notes: 2026-10-22 (clockwork-courier-p5): the rope bridge and seesaw of rooftops_3 fall or take 7% more frames after other test files; storage, session and module state were reset, so the order dependence seems to live in the physics world. Workaround: heavier plank damping (scripts/rope_bridge.js), narrower seesaw waypoints (tests/helpers/routes.js), a 10 percent tolerance in tests/levels.test.js.

2026-10-22 (engine): root cause was Physics3D solving Joint3D constraints in the order of their owner entity bits (a std::map), i.e. in the history of the World (slot reuse, earlier scenes), and Physics3D::reset() keeping joint state. Joints are now solved in body creation order (the scene order) and reset() drops them. Same scene gives bit-identical poses whatever ran before. The tolerance in tests/levels.test.js is removed; the damping and waypoints stay as gameplay.

entries.title: Products.storekit exists only with a built Apple plugin and has one locale
entries.missing: factoria export --platform ios writes Products.storekit only when the Apple plugin is declared AND built (plugins/apple/ios/*/libapple.a), so a game that has not run platform.add_backend on a Mac gets no local StoreKit file and no hint that the catalog was skipped. The file has one en_US localization: the titleKey translations (es) never reach it. P6 (clockwork-courier-p6) hit it again: platform.add_backend apple on the real project (a Mac with Xcode tools) wrote plugins/apple and the next ios export wrote Products.storekit; Xcode opens it only from that file, so the in-app purchase check could not be done in the simulator by the export alone.
entries.workaround: Checked on a scratch copy: add_backend apple, cmake build of the plugin, export; the four products came out right (ids, types, prices). The real project does not declare the plugin.
entries.suggestion: Write Products.storekit whenever the catalog has products and the target is ios (the plugin only matters for the scheme), and one localization per locale of the project, from titleKey.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.19 (Export and store material checks) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/export-checks (M26.19): every iOS export whose catalog has products writes Products.storekit, with or without the Apple plugin, with one localization per language of the project from titleKey / descriptionKey.

entries.title: Scripts cannot see the app being suspended, resumed or losing focus
entries.missing: A phone game must pause when the app goes to the background or the window loses focus. The native player gets Suspended/Resumed events but JavaScript has no hook (no game.onSuspend, no app focus state), so a game cannot pause itself or silence music by the book.
entries.workaround: scripts/comfort.js watches time.unscaledDt: a single frame longer than 0.75 s means the app was away, and it opens the pause menu. It cannot tell a suspend from a long hitch and cannot react before the suspend.
entries.suggestion: Expose game.onSuspend/onResume (and window focus) to scripts, and have a project setting that pauses the game on suspend by default.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.3 (Calendar date and app lifecycle) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/calendar-lifecycle (M26.3): game.on("suspend"|"resume"|"focus"|"blur"), game.focused, and pauseOnSuspend (default true) pause the game and the music in the background.

entries.title: No graphics quality API: no render scale, no GPU info and the frame cap throws on phones
entries.missing: Graphics quality presets need a render scale (or MSAA) and the device tier. From JavaScript there is no render scale setter, no way to read the GPU or whether the device is low end, and window.frameCap throws on a phone, so a frame cap option has to be hidden there with a platform guess.
entries.workaround: The quality preset (scripts/accessibility.js) only changes what scripts own: Light.castShadows, view distance fog, particle counts and lantern lights. The frame cap option is disabled on phones (scripts/ui/options.js) and a phone starts at medium quality by a screen-size guess (scripts/settings.js).
entries.suggestion: Add window.renderScale (0.5..1) and a read-only game.deviceTier or gpu info, and make window.frameCap a no-op that returns the real cap on phones instead of throwing.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.15 (Graphics quality and render stats) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/render-quality (M26.15): window.renderScale (0.5..1), window.supports("frameCap" | "renderScale" | ...) and game.device {formFactor, gpuBackend, memoryGB, tier} (fixed values headless, game.setDevice in tests). The frame cap still throws on a phone, so the options screen reads window.supports("frameCap"); the presets set renderScale and a new player starts at game.device.tier instead of a screen-size guess.

entries.title: Slider value set from a script sends no ui.change and shows the raw number
entries.missing: Setting Slider.value from a script does not raise ui.change, so tests cannot drive a slider except by clicking its track at a position they have to compute. A Slider with min/max shows the plain value in its value column (for example 1) and has no format option, so a percentage or unit cannot be shown.
entries.workaround: tests/comfort.test.js clicks the middle of the track and checks the saved value is inside the range; the options show the multiplier as a plain number.
entries.suggestion: Add a test helper game.setSlider(id, value) that behaves like the user, and Slider.format (for example "{value:0%}").
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.18 (Slider and ScrollList) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: The test API cannot observe a quit request
entries.missing: game.quit() in a test really stops the engine and every later test fails; game.state() in the test API has no quitRequested although the game.state command has it. (The state that leaks between tests is FB-0026.)
entries.workaround: tests/comfort.test.js patches the quit function of the engine object for the duration of the test and restores it.
entries.suggestion: Add game.quitRequested to the test API and make game.quit() only set it in tests.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: No locale-aware number formatting
entries.missing: i18n.t fills {placeholders} with String(value): a decimal always has a point, there are no thousands separators, no ordinals and no locale rule for time or list formatting. Spanish needs 1,5 and 1:15,0.
entries.workaround: Each locale file states format.decimal and scripts/fmt.js applies it (decimal, clock) before the value goes into i18n.t.
entries.suggestion: Number, percent and duration formatters in i18n (i18n.number(v, {digits}), i18n.duration) following the active language, and {value:number} style placeholders.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.13 (Locale-aware numbers) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: TouchButton has no localization key
entries.missing: TouchButton.text cannot take `key`, so its label stays in one language and a language switch does not rewrite it.
entries.workaround: scripts/hud.js writes the label in the current language at start and at every i18n change, and sizes the font to fit the 96 px disc.
entries.suggestion: A `key` field on TouchButton, like Text and Button.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.12 (Localized text with parameters) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/i18n-args (M26.12): TouchButton has key and keyArgs like the other widgets; hud.js sets the key and the engine rewrites the label at every language switch.

entries.title: Toggle and Slider labels do not wrap or shrink
entries.missing: A Toggle or Slider label never wraps (Button does with maxWidth). A Slider with autoSize and a long label grows to about 1800 px at 200 percent text in Spanish; with a fixed size the label overlaps the track.
entries.workaround: Sliders are fixed size with an empty label and a Text above each one (maxWidth wraps it); the options list width follows ui.textScale (fitWidth in scripts/ui/options.js); the Toggle labels stay short in every locale.
entries.suggestion: maxWidth on Toggle and Slider (wrap the label, grow the height), and a Slider label placed above the track.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.6 (Text that fits) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/text-fits (M26.6): Toggle.maxWidth and Slider.maxWidth wrap the label, Slider.labelAbove puts it above the track; options.prefab.json uses them (no name Texts, no fitWidth in options.js).

entries.title: No shrink-to-fit or per-screen text scale cap
entries.missing: ui.textScale multiplies every screen-space text, but widgets that sit at fixed places or have a fixed size (cards, HUD rows, headings, round touch buttons) clip or overlap at 200 percent, and Spanish and Japanese labels differ in length from English. There is no autoShrink on Text or Button, no per-entity scale cap and no way to know a label overflowed.
entries.workaround: Four screens cap the effective size of their fixed-place texts in script (level_select capSizes, hud layoutHud, touch labels in hud.js, toast panel fit); menus use fit Panels with fallbackLayout and ScrollLists with fill.
entries.suggestion: Text.autoShrink (minFontSize) and Button.autoShrink, plus Widget.maxTextScale so a heading or a disc label can stop growing.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.6 (Text that fits) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/text-fits (M26.6): Text, Button, Toggle, Slider and TouchButton have autoShrink (minFontSize) and maxTextScale, and ui.overflowed(id) reports a label that still does not fit; level_select.js, hud.js and the touch labels use them instead of rewriting font sizes (toast.js keeps its fit Panel and gets maxTextScale).

entries.title: No overflow or pseudo-localisation check
entries.missing: validate checks glyph coverage but not whether a translated label fits its widget; layout problems at 200 percent or in a long language were found only by looking at screenshots one by one.
entries.workaround: A tour script drove factoria session through every screen per language and scale and listed widgets whose ui.state rect left the screen; tests/i18n.test.js repeats the key screens.
entries.suggestion: `factoria validate --pseudo-loc` (or a ui.overflowing() query) that lists clipped labels and widgets outside the screen at a given text scale and language.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.23 (UI layout check) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/layout-check (M26.23): `ui.check_layout` loads each scene in each language and text scale plus a pseudo-localized pass and lists overflowing, overlapping and off-screen texts. First run on the game found the profile keyboard keys and the intro title and Skip button overflowing at 200 % (fixed with autoShrink); still open in the game: intro_hint leaves the screen at 200 % (safeArea bottom anchor), intro_hint overlaps intro_skip in Spanish at 200 %, select_title overlaps select_total at 200 % in every language, and the pseudo pass shows the main menu title and the Shop, Leaderboards and Credits buttons breaking at 200 % with 40 % longer text.

entries.title: A headless test cannot set the system language
entries.missing: i18n.systemLanguages is always empty headless and no test hook sets it, so the first-run language choice (system language, else default) cannot be tested end to end; game.setAccessibility exists for the text size but nothing for the language.
entries.workaround: The rule is a pure function, settings.pickLanguage(systemLanguages, supported, fallback), tested with lists; the engine's own pick is not exercised.
entries.suggestion: game.setSystemLanguages([...]) in the test API, like setAccessibility, applied by the next scene load.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.11 (Test API gaps) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: assets.set_provenance re-sorts the whole assets.json
entries.missing: Recording one asset's provenance rewrites and re-sorts every entry of assets.json, so a one-line change is a diff of the whole file and conflicts with parallel work.
entries.workaround: The font entry was inserted by hand in assets.json, in the same shape.
entries.suggestion: Keep the file order and touch only the entry.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.5 (Model import and asset tooling) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/model-import (M26.5): assets.set_provenance (every assets.json edit) keeps the order of the file and changes only the entry; a hand-ordered file gets new entries appended, a sorted one stays sorted.

entries.title: A fill ScrollList makes its whole panel screen-tall
entries.missing: A fit Panel that contains a ScrollList with fill becomes exactly as tall as the screen, whatever the list holds, so a short list leaves a big empty panel and the Panel can no longer centre on its content.
entries.workaround: Each list gets a design size and fill: the panel uses the screen height only when the content is taller (credits, achievements, leaderboards, shop, options).
entries.suggestion: fill should take only the room left (maxHeight = screen minus the other rows), and let the panel shrink below it.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.18 (Slider and ScrollList) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: platform.add_backend ignores dryRun and rewrites the whole factoria.json
entries.missing: platform.add_backend {"backend":"apple","dryRun":true} still wrote plugins/apple/ and the "plugins" entry, and the factoria.json came back reformatted (every array re-indented), so the diff of one added block is hundreds of lines.
entries.workaround: Kept the real result (it is what makes the export write Products.storekit) and committed it; the reformatting is in the same commit as the plugin.
entries.suggestion: Honour dryRun (print what would be written) and edit factoria.json in place without reformatting. Also exclude plugins/apple/build from the folder it creates, or say it is a build dir to ignore.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.1 (Commands write only what they change) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/commands-write-only (M26.1): `platform.add_backend` and `project.new_plugin` patch only `plugins.<name>` in factoria.json (key order and layout kept), take `dryRun`, refuse unknown arguments with a did-you-mean, and plugin templates have a .gitignore.

entries.title: Android export needs the exact CMake 3.31.6 in the SDK and a JDK, with no offline way around it
entries.missing: factoria export --platform android (source mode) failed because the SDK had no CMake 3.31.6 (Gradle tries to download it) and the machine had no JAVA_HOME. The error says what is missing but not how to point at another CMake or JDK.
entries.workaround: Scratch scripts outside the repo: a cmake.dir in local.properties pointing at the system CMake (4.4.4), -Pfactoria.cmakeVersion=4.4.4 and JAVA_HOME from a JDK that was already installed (the one bundled with Unity Hub); then Gradle --offline built a 52.8 MB apk in 2m23s.
entries.suggestion: Accept any CMake >= the minimum (read from `cmake --version` or `export.android.cmake`), print the cmake.dir / JAVA_HOME / --offline recipe in the error, and let `factoria doctor` list both.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: the JDK is already found (JAVA_HOME, Android Studio's, PATH); CMake must still be the SDK's 3.31.6: work package M26.19 (Export and store material checks) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/export-checks (M26.19): the Android source build reads the CMake it will use (the SDK's 3.31.6, else the newest 3.24+ in the SDK, else one of the computer through cmake.dir in local.properties and factoria.cmakeVersion in gradle.properties); the error hint gives the offline recipe. The JDK was already found (JAVA_HOME, Android Studio, PATH).

entries.title: Desktop export does not check that the bundled player matches the factoria that exports
entries.missing: factoria export --platform macos bundles the factoria_player next to the factoria binary and says nothing about its version. Here that player was once a build six days older than factoria: the --release app stopped with "no factoria.json in '/'" and the normal app did not know Text.key, Text.safeArea or Button (scripts/intro.js threw "not a function"). With a player built from the same checkout both apps run from '/' (game.pak found in Contents/Resources, Apple backend ready, exit 0), so the engine's lookup works; what is missing is the check.
entries.workaround: Rebuilt the engine so factoria and factoria_player match (or pass --player <build dir>/player/factoria_player) and exported again; macOS verified running. SHIPPING.md says how to check.
entries.suggestion: Print the player path and version in the export report, and warn (or refuse without --allow-player-mismatch) when the player's version or build id differs from the factoria that exports. The Windows export already reads the player's version information; do the same on macOS and Linux (factoria_player --version).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open; work package M26.19 (Export and store material checks) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/export-checks (M26.19): factoria and factoria_player carry a build fingerprint; a desktop export with a player from another build stops with an error naming both builds, and --allow-player-mismatch (allowPlayerMismatch) bundles it anyway.

entries.title: perf.measure and the test API give no triangles or lights, and renderStats is zero headless
entries.missing: A render budget for a phone wants triangles, lights, texture memory and draw calls. perf.measure reports only draw calls and entities; game.state.renderStats is all zeros in a headless call; the test API cannot read draw calls at all.
entries.workaround: tests/budget.test.js counts entities, MeshRenderer, Light and ParticleEmitter of every level in the running scene (static numbers); perf.json holds the draw-call budget of the heaviest level.
entries.suggestion: Add triangles, lights, shadowCasters and textureMB to perf.measure and to a `game.renderStats()` in factoria:test (the headless EGL/Metal renderer has them after one frame).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: game.renderStats exists but stays zero until a frame is drawn, which a headless test may never do, and perf.measure records no triangles or lights: work package M26.15 (Graphics quality and render stats) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/render-quality (M26.15): game.renderStats() in tests draws a frame when none was drawn and adds shadowCasters and textureMB; perf.measure records triangles, lights and textureMB; perf.check takes budgets (maxTriangles...). tests/budget.test.js checks real triangles, lights, shadow casters and draw calls (falling back to scene counts without a GPU) and perf.json holds budgets.

entries.title: No video playback, and --record-video writes a very large AVI
entries.missing: A studio intro or a store trailer is a video file in most games; the engine cannot play one, and --record-video writes an AVI of 183 MB for 43.6 s at 1280x720 that every store needs converted (ffmpeg is not part of the toolchain).
entries.workaround: The intro is an animated scene (scenes/intro.scene.json, scripts/intro.js). The trailer is a scripted director scene recorded with --record-video; SHIPPING.md has the ffmpeg command to make the mp4.
entries.suggestion: A Video component (mp4/webm with the platform decoder) and an --record-video output that is already H.264 mp4 when the OS offers an encoder (VideoToolbox, Media Foundation, MediaCodec).
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: --record-video trailer.mp4 already writes H.264 + AAC when ffmpeg is found (b54e313, before this report; docs/CLI.md); installing ffmpeg is work package M26.19 (Export and store material checks) in feedback/ROADMAP.md, and playing a video is M19's video item in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

2026-10-23: fixed in m26/export-checks (M26.19) in part: `factoria setup ffmpeg` (setup.install component ffmpeg, listed by setup.status) installs a pinned ffmpeg so --record-video trailer.mp4 writes H.264 + AAC with no manual step. Still open: playing a video in a game (M19's video item in feedback/ROADMAP.md).

entries.title: Web player: typing in a TextInput from the browser pane did not fill it
entries.missing: In the web export opened in a browser pane, key events sent with the pane's typing tool did not put letters in the name field of the name screen (the on-screen keyboard buttons did). It may be the pane's synthetic events rather than the player, and there is no documented way to tell.
entries.workaround: Filled the name with the on-screen keyboard of the game (scripts/profile.js) for the check.
entries.suggestion: Document how the web player receives text (keydown vs the text input event, hidden input element for mobile keyboards) so a game can test it, and add an autotest page to the web player.
notes: 2026-10-23: Fixed in M26.17: the web player has a hidden input for mobile browsers, TEXT.md and EXPORTING.md describe typing, and the web smoke types into a field (run by CI).

2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: the web player takes typed text from the browser's keypress events, which a browser pane's synthetic key events may not send, so this is probably not a player bug; the docs, a web autotest and a hidden input for mobile keyboards are work package M26.17 (Text entry on every device) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: No warning when a dynamic body starts inside a static collider
entries.missing: The rope bridges of rooftops_3 and market_3 started with their end planks 0.15 m inside the roof slabs. The engine pushed them out with no log line, the hinge chain buckled upwards and never settled, and the levels played differently on Linux CI than on this Mac. It took a day of tracing plank positions to find.
entries.workaround: Moved both ends of each bridge 0.2 m off the slabs and wrote the rule in the header of scripts/rope_bridge.js.

notes: 2026-10-22 triage: duplicate of FB-0015 (no warning for a body that starts inside a static collider; its occurrences were merged there); work package M26.14 (Joints: overlaps, rest and bridges) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.

entries.title: Joint3D chains never come fully to rest and unrelated chains affect each other
entries.missing: A chain of 9 hinged planks with linearDamping 8 and angularDamping 30 keeps trembling about 4 cm and never falls asleep. The state of the rope bridge also changes how the see-saw (another joint group far away, not touching it) moves, so a fix in one part of a level shifts the timing of another.
entries.workaround: None in the engine: the autoplay route crosses the see-saw with smaller, more careful steps (tests/helpers/routes.js).
entries.suggestion: Let jointed bodies sleep as a group once all of them are calm, and solve separate joint islands independently so one island cannot disturb another.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: confirmed open: jointed bodies never sleep and a CCD event far away holds every body of the world (physics3d.cpp); the dependence on earlier tests was CC/FB-0033, fixed in M25. Work package M26.14 (Joints: overlaps, rest and bridges) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
2026-10-23: fixed in m26/joints (M26.14): Joint3D.damping, chain iterations and drag: the rope bridge needs no heavy damping or wide planks.

entries.title: 3D physics is not identical across platforms
entries.missing: The same level, input and seed gave different results on Linux (GCC, x86-64) and macOS (Clang, arm64): the courier fell off a rope bridge on Linux CI and not on the Mac. A chaotic setup turns floating-point differences into a different game, so a test that passes on one platform fails on another, and replays recorded on one platform drift on another.
entries.workaround: Made the bridges settle (ends off the slabs) and checked the level route under small position nudges (±0.2 mm to ±1.5 cm of every plank and of the courier) so it passes whatever the rounding.
entries.suggestion: Document that physics is deterministic per build, not across platforms; offer a robustness check (run a test N times with tiny perturbations) so games find chaotic spots before CI does; consider strict floating point (no FMA contraction) in the physics module.
notes: 2026-10-22 triage: holds in part: the 3D physics is the engine's own (no Jolt) and is deterministic for one build on one platform, which the docs do not say; work package M26.21 (Physics determinism across platforms) in feedback/ROADMAP.md.
